subject: Specifying the number of starting values

messages.author: ab08386cc5e71286
messages.subject: Specifying the number of starting values
parts:
Hello,

is it possible to specify the number of starting values in a CFA in R lavaan? In Mplus this can be done by "ANALYSIS: starts =", is there a similar command in lavaan?

Thank you,
Noell

messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: Specifying the number of starting values
parts:
Noell,
I have done this before but unfortunately I am currently unable to locate the code to share with you.  My strategy was this:

1. Use the lavaanify() function to extract the parameter table from your model.
2. Write a function that selects random start values for parameters using desired distributions (e.g., runif() or rnorm()).  If several parameters come from the same distribution, generate the values as a vector.
3. Insert the random values into the start value column of the parameter table in the corresponding rows (using indexing with square brackets).
4. Fit the model using this parameter table in place of the model syntax.
5. If needed, place this all into a loop to run multiple samples of start values in a single call of your function.  Save the lavaan object output in a list and return that.  Make the number of fits a parameter to the function for convenience.

Sorry I do not have the sample code at my fingertips.

Keith

Hi Noell,

Personally, I prefer the approach by Keith. Nevertheless, if you like to do it using lavaan syntax, use start(), as illustrated below.

``` r
# Adapted from the example of lavaan::cfa()
library(lavaan)
#> This is lavaan 0.6-16
#> lavaan is FREE software! Please report any bugs.
# "Multiply" a parameter by start(x), x being the starting value.
HS.model <- ' visual  =~ x1 + start(1.2) * x2 + start(1.3) * x3
              speed   =~ x7 + start(0.8) * x8 + start(0.7) * x9 '

fit <- cfa(HS.model, data = HolzingerSwineford1939)
parameterEstimates(fit)
#>       lhs op    rhs   est    se      z pvalue ci.lower ci.upper
#> 1  visual =~     x1 1.000 0.000     NA     NA    1.000    1.000
#> 2  visual =~     x2 0.690 0.124  5.585      0    0.448    0.932

#> 4   speed =~     x7 1.000 0.000     NA     NA    1.000    1.000
#> 5   speed =~     x8 1.204 0.170  7.090      0    0.871    1.536
#> 6   speed =~     x9 1.052 0.147  7.142      0    0.763    1.340
#> 7      x1 ~~     x1 0.754 0.110  6.838      0    0.538    0.971
#> 8      x2 ~~     x2 1.094 0.103 10.661      0    0.893    1.296
#> 9      x3 ~~     x3 0.688 0.105  6.557      0    0.483    0.894

#> 15 visual ~~  speed 0.223 0.052  4.290      0    0.121    0.324
```

messages.author: ff3a366aa7a9b488
messages.subject: Re: Specifying the number of starting values
parts:
As a supplement to Keith and Shu Fai. You can also take advantage of the fact that the lavaan model syntax is usually a string. Something like this (quick and dirty):

library(lavaan)

model <- "
visual  =~ x1 + start(%s.x2%) * x2 + start(%s.x3%) * x3
speed   =~ x7 + start(%s.x8%) * x8 + start(%s.x9%) * x9
"

pattern     <- c("%s.x2%", "%s.x3%", "%s.x8%", "%s.x9%")
replacement <- function(pattern) runif(length(pattern))
nRep        <- 3

lapply(1 : nRep, function(x, model, pattern, replacement) {
  gsub.rec <- function(a, b, model) if(length(a) == 0) model else gsub.rec(a[-1], b[-1], gsub(a[1], b[1], model, fixed = TRUE))
  cfa(gsub.rec(pattern, replacement, model), data = HolzingerSwineford1939)
}, model, pattern, replacement(pattern))


This should do roughly what Keith suggests.
